Copy index.html beside a page's content.yaml — figure.html is the obvious name — and paste the section below into that page's contents with data: changed to match. Or copy this whole directory into pages/<parent>/children/<name>/ and it draws as it stands.

The picture is held while the prose scrolls past it, and it is released where this section ends: sticky only pins inside its own containing block. That is why the figure and the argument are ONE section rather than two.

The figure is a drawing and not a photograph. A row of counts over a row of bars, in HTML, on the palette's tokens, growing once when the section is first seen — which is what a figure is here. Its words and its numbers are the section's variables, as parallel lists, so changing the drawing is changing the document.

What the section can do that the document could not

A section is a div. It is full width, it owns its layout entirely, and the reading measure lives inside the default section's own file rather than on the sheet — so a band that goes edge to edge costs nothing, and a column that wants 34rem of measure asks for it here.

Prose still wants a measure. A page that is edge to edge everywhere is exactly as monotonous as one that is 34rem everywhere.

The freedom is to choose per section. Two columns where a figure earns its place beside the argument; one column where the words are the whole of it; a grid where things are being compared. A page that chooses the same shape every time has not used any of it.

Swap this slot's prose for the real argument, and swap kpiName, kpiValue, barName and barValue for the real figures. The tallest bar lights itself, so nothing here has to be told which one matters.
